en: The sampaguita, the national flower of the Philippines, is a specific species of jasmine known scientifically as Jasminum sambac.
The carabao, the national animal of the Philippines, is a domesticated swamp buffalo scientifically named Bubalus bubalis carabanesis.
The legislative branch of the Philippine government makes laws and is called Congress, consisting of the Senate and House of Representatives.
Jose Rizal, a Philippine national hero, wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses.
The Philippines declared independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite, under the leadership of Emilio Aguinaldo.
The Igorot people are indigenous groups in the Cordillera Administrative Region known for building the ancient Banaue Rice Terraces.
Filipino, the national language of the Philippines, is primarily based on Tagalog and is written using the Latin alphabet.
Pithecophaga jefferyi, the Philippine eagle, is the national bird and a critically endangered raptor endemic to the country.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño through a rhythmic two-steps forward, one-step backward dance.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School and founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines.
Under the Philippine Constitution, every citizen has the right to vote in elections once they reach the age of eighteen.
The Filipino value of bayanihan refers to the traditional practice of a community working together to physically relocate a nipa hut.
